To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed model is a valuable tool for the evaluation of CSR commitment and for the identification of material CSR issues.

(i) the proposed model is based on the classification and analysis of customer CSR feedback, (ii) the model can be extended to any stakeholder and it is useful to identify material CSR issues and to engage stakeholders, (iii) the model is based on a comparison of three aspects (disclosed, expected and perceived) of CSR commitment.
a feedback-based model for the assessment of CSR commitment and materiality analysis can be developed and applied to any stakeholder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to identify and assess material CSR issues through customer feedback.
how to engage stakeholders in a CSR dialogue and to what extent their CSR perceptions and expectations should be considered in a firm's CSR strategy.
the following questions: What is the relationship between the three aspects of CSR?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper proposes an original model that can be applied in the context of stakeholder engagement for materiality analysis.
the proposed model is a valid and effective tool for materiality analysis, CSR planning and stakeholder engagement, and it is a useful instrument to assess and classify CSR feedback.
the model is a useful tool for CSR evaluation and materiality analysis and can be applied to any stakeholder, not just to customers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model provides a useful framework for CSR evaluation, materiality analysis and planning.
the proposed model provides a useful tool for the identification of CSR issues that are relevant for a company’s stakeholders.
we provide a new model for CSR evaluation based on customer feedback, and that we show how to use this model to engage stakeholders in a materiality analysis and in the definition of CSR priorities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

CSR materiality analysis should not be limited to a mere analysis of the firm’s disclosed information, as it is often the case, but should be extended to a more comprehensive analysis of all stakeholder expectations and perceptions, which can be done through the use of a feedback-based model.

a CSR assessment based on the classification and comparison of three aspects (disclosed, expected and perceived) of the stakeholder CSR commitment allows the identification of the material CSR issues and the development of a more effective CSR strategy.
the model provides a useful instrument to identify the materiality of CSR issues, which is a key element of any CSR strategy.
